Work in /opt/nxeon (Proxmox host running a VPS hosting platform going customer-ready). You are fixing BACKUPS — the platform's own data currently exists in exactly one place on one machine. Read `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` (finding P0-9 and P1 backup items) and `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` for context. Do not edit either.

VERIFIED FACTS (I checked the live box — trust these over any assumption):
- DB backups WORK: `scripts/backup-db.sh` → `/tank/backup/db`, daily 03:15, 10 files present, 14-day retention.
- **Whole-VM backups have NEVER RUN.** `systemctl show nxeon-backup-vms.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp` is EMPTY. Timer is `Sun 04:31` weekly. Find out WHY it never fired and fix that root cause — do not just change the schedule.
- The only archives in `/tank/backup/dump` are a CUSTOMER's own backups of vmid 102. No platform backups exist.
- Off-site (`scripts/backup-offsite.sh`) runs daily and exits 0 with "NOT CONFIGURED"; `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` has every target commented out.
- Proxmox storage `backup` = 3.7 TB, 0.06% used. Real paths: `/tank/backup/db`, `/tank/backup/dump`.
- `nxeon-verify-restore.timer` last ran 2026-07-24.

YOU OWN EXACTLY: `lib/proxmox.ts`, `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `scripts/backup-*.sh`, `scripts/verify-restore.sh` (if present), systemd unit/timer/drop-in files for `nxeon-backup-*`, a NEW `app/admin/backups/page.tsx` plus new components under `components/admin/` that only it uses, and ONE minimal nav-entry edit in `app/admin/layout.tsx`. `prisma/schema.prisma` is FROZEN. Do NOT touch `worker/index.ts`, `lib/order.ts`, or anything else.

FIX, in priority order:

**1. DATA-LOSS BUG.** `lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` `pruneBackups` filters only on `vmid` across the whole shared `backup` storage. So a CUSTOMER's manual backup prunes and DELETES the platform's own host-level VM backups for that same vmid, written by `scripts/backup-vms.sh`. Make customer pruning provably unable to touch platform archives — distinguish them (vzdump `--notes-template`, a filename marker, or a separate storage/prefix) rather than best-effort. State in your report exactly why it is now impossible, not merely unlikely.

**2. Make whole-system backups actually happen, at the owner's stated cadence:** "back up the entire system once every day, store the latest 3." Today: VM timer weekly keeping 2 (drop-in `NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP=2`), DB retention 14 days. Make VM backups DAILY keeping 3. Also back up `/etc/pve` — nothing does, and without it a bare-metal rebuild loses every VM definition.

**3. Off-site.** `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` must FAIL LOUDLY and visibly when unconfigured instead of exiting 0 pretending success — an inert backup that reports OK is worse than none, and it has been "succeeding" daily for days. Document precisely what the owner must set (`OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` or `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET`).

**4. NEW ADMIN PAGE `/admin/backups`.** The owner asked "where are the backups for the entire server?" and the answer was: there is no such page. Build it — DB dumps and VM archives read from disk/`pvesm` (path, size, age, which VM), every backup timer's last-run and next-run with any that have **NEVER run** flagged loudly (that would have caught this), off-site configured-or-not shown prominently with last successful sync, and restore-verification status. Match the Nxeon dark theme exactly: reuse `.card`, `PageHeader`, `Badge`, `StatusDot`, existing slate/brand/navy classes; invent no new visual styles. Gate it with the same `requireArea(...)` pattern the other admin pages use.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- This is a LIVE production host with real customer VMs. NEVER delete a backup, never run `vzdump` for real, never start/restart/daemon-reload a service. You may EDIT unit files — I will apply them. Read-only commands (`pvesm status`, `ls`, `systemctl show`, `journalctl`) are fine.
- Do NOT run `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`.
- Do NOT git commit or push. Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma. Do NOT write to the live database.
- Comment style: explain WHY and cite the real failure prevented.

Report: the root cause of why VM backups never ran, exactly how customer pruning is now safe, the new cadences, what the owner must set for off-site, and any systemd files I need to apply.

1	# Nxeon — Pre-launch QA audit
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-25 · **Scope:** customer portal, admin portal, backend (`lib/**`, `worker/**`, `app/api/**`)
4	**Method:** source review, read-only inspection of the live `nxeon` database, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and
5	cross-checking the Proxmox perl source on this host. Nothing in this audit modified code, services, or data.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Executive summary
10	
11	### The single most dangerous issue
12	
13	**Any customer who can afford the cheapest email plan can take over another customer's email domain,
14	reset the password on their live mailboxes, and read and send mail as them.**
15	
16	`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-257` scopes the "one subscription per domain" check to the *caller*:
17	
18	```ts
19	const dupe = await db.emailSubscription.findFirst({
20	  where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } },
21	});
22	```
23	
24	There is no check that another user already holds that domain, no `@@unique` on
25	`EmailSubscription.domainName` (`prisma/schema.prisma:604`), no `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`
26	(`:623`), and no `sub.verified` gate on any mailbox mutation. Every Mailcow call is keyed by the
27	**address string** on one shared Mailcow instance, so `resetMailboxPassword` (`:706`) rewrites the
28	password of whatever real mailbox that string names — and hands the plaintext back to the caller.
29	
30	Mailcow is configured in production (`MAILCOW_API_URL` + `MAILCOW_API_KEY` are both set), and the live
31	DB holds two active subscriptions with real mailboxes — including `admin@revsports.ca`, the platform's
32	own `BASE_DOMAIN`, which receives Nxeon's own password-reset mail. This is exploitable today, by any
33	signed-up user, in three clicks. Full detail in **P0-1**.
34	
35	### Go / no-go
36	
37	**NO-GO for paying customers.** Fix P0-1 through P0-8 first; they are the launch blockers.
38	
39	This is not a verdict on the codebase's quality — much of it is genuinely better than typical for this
40	stage. The wallet ledger is atomic and race-safe (`lib/wallet.ts` conditional `updateMany`, CAS on
41	`expiresAt` in every renewal path). Ownership checks are present and correct on **all 20+ mutating
42	server actions and all 35 API routes** — two independent passes found no IDOR in the server/domain/
43	volume/website/database/file surfaces. `lib/ssh-exec.ts` is a reject-don't-sanitize allowlist with
44	mandatory timeouts and secrets confined to STDIN; **no command injection was found anywhere**, and
45	that was looked for hard. Disk shrink is blocked at four independent layers. `qm destroy` is reachable
46	only through a `Server` row. Job claiming is atomic. GDPR deletion re-validates server-side.
47	
48	The problems are concentrated in four themes:
49	
50	* **9 P0s.** One live cross-tenant email takeover; one unauthenticated 2FA-verification endpoint; two
51	  paths that silently destroy customer volumes; a Stripe flow that can take money and provision
52	  nothing; proration that overcharges by up to $379; refunds that are untraceable and non-idempotent;
53	  a suspension path that permanently deletes a *paid-up* customer's VM; and a "Daily auto-backups"
54	  add-on that never produces a single backup.
55	* **A large "furniture" surface — the dominant defect class in this codebase.** ~18 admin settings are
56	  written to the DB and read by nothing (the dunning controls, the referral reward, the domain markup —
57	  which displays 0% while customers are charged 25%), and the customer portal has a matching set:
58	  notification preferences, SSL auto-renew, WHOIS privacy, custom nameservers, registrar lock, team
59	  permissions, affiliate tiers, mail Reply-To and the API `write` scope are all persisted, all
60	  confirmed with a green "Saved", and all read by nothing. **Every one of these tells the user a
61	  guarantee is in force when it is not.**
62	* **Whole features that cannot work today**: plan downgrades (blocked by a guard no live plan pair can
63	  satisfy), coupons (redemption UI hidden whenever Stripe is on), bandwidth metering (and therefore the
64	  entire abuse-detection subsystem built on it), 4 of the 5 one-click apps, and game settings.
65	* **One availability landmine**: a single hung job wedges the entire platform's queue, forever.
66	
67	A useful signal for triage: the team already knows how to handle an unfinished feature correctly.
68	`components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx` is deliberately **not rendered**, with the reason documented in
69	`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:11-15` — *"the feature is unwired … so we don't expose it and promise
70	something that does nothing."* That is exactly the right call. Roughly 25 findings below are the same
71	situation handled the other way.
72	
73	**Counts:** P0 · 9 · P1 · 42 · P2 · 19 · P3 · 15
74	
75	---
76	
77	# P0 — money and data
78	
79	## P0-1. Cross-tenant email domain takeover — live and exploitable today
80	
81	**Files:** `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-257`, `:491-539`, `:684-722`, `:81-122`;
82	`prisma/schema.prisma:600-626`; `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:88-94`
83	
84	Four defects compose into a full takeover:
85	
86	1. **Caller-scoped duplicate check** (`:254-257`) — a second user can claim a domain another customer
87	   already has a subscription for.
88	2. **No DB-level uniqueness** — `EmailSubscription.domainName` and `Mailbox.address` are both plain
89	   `String`. Nothing stops the second claim.
90	3. **`sub.verified` is never checked before any mailbox mutation.** `addMailbox` (`:499`) gates only
91	   on `sub.userId === user.id`, and its address-collision check (`:514`) only looks at
92	   `sub.mailboxes` — the *attacker's own* subscription's mailboxes. It cannot see the victim's.
93	4. **Mailcow is addressed by string, not by an identifier we own.**
94	
95	**Exploit** (attacker = any signed-up user with enough balance for the cheapest email plan):
96	
97	1. `orderEmailHosting("victim.com", planId)` → accepted (`external: true, verified: false`).
98	2. `addMailbox(subId, "ceo")` → row created with `address = "ceo@victim.com"`. If the mailbox already
99	   exists in Mailcow the create fails and the row lands `FAILED` — **but the row persists with the
100	   victim's address.**
101	3. `resetMailboxPassword(mailboxId)` → `:706` `mcSetMailboxPassword(mailbox.address, password)`
102	   rewrites the password on the **real, live** mailbox and returns the plaintext to the attacker.
103	   Full IMAP/SMTP/webmail: read the victim's mail, and send as them with Nxeon's SPF/DKIM alignment.
104	   `resolveMailbox` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:90`) also resolves it, so the built-in webmail works.
105	
106	**Variants, same root cause:**
107	* **Destruction** — `removeMailbox` (`:588`) `mcDeleteMailbox(mailbox.address)` deletes the victim's
108	  mailbox and all stored mail; the error is swallowed and the attacker's row is dropped.
109	* **Denial of service** — `setMailboxSuspended` (`:617`).
110	* **Silent interception** — `ownedDomains()` (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:88-94`) treats an
111	  **unverified** subscription as proof of domain control, so `mcAddAlias` can forward inbound mail.
112	* **Spoofing any domain** — `:95-98` calls `mcCreateDomain(domain)` for any claimed name, making the
113	  shared Mailcow authoritative for domains the attacker doesn't own. Independent IP-reputation risk.
114	
115	**Fix.** (a) Add `@@unique([domainName])` on `EmailSubscription` (excluding CANCELLED via a partial
116	index or a status-aware guard) and `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`. (b) Make the duplicate check global,
117	not caller-scoped. (c) Refuse **every** mailbox/alias mutation unless `sub.verified === true`, and
118	require DNS proof-of-control before verification for `external` domains. (d) Before any Mailcow write,
119	re-assert that the address's domain belongs to a verified subscription owned by the caller.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## P0-2. `verifyTotpForUser` is an unauthenticated, unthrottled 2FA oracle
124	
125	**File:** `lib/actions-2fa.ts:50-71` (file is `"use server"` at `:1`)
126	
127	```ts
128	export async function verifyTotpForUser(userId: string, code: string): Promise<boolean> {
129	  const user = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
130	  ...
131	```
132	
133	Every export of a `"use server"` module is a registered, callable server action. This one takes an
134	arbitrary `userId`, performs **no authentication, no ownership check and no rate limit**, returns a
135	raw boolean, and **mutates state** — a matching backup code is consumed and deleted (`:62-63`).
136	
137	`login` (`lib/actions.ts:157`) is throttled to 10 attempts per 15 min per email+IP. Calling this action
138	directly bypasses that entirely: unlimited TOTP and backup-code guessing against a named account.
139	Victim `userId`s are readily obtainable — `inviteMember` (`lib/actions-teams.ts:110`) creates a
140	Membership **without the invitee's consent**, and `app/dashboard/team/page.tsx:42-47` then hands the
141	attacker every co-member's `userId` and email.
142	
143	The action's ID does not currently appear in any client chunk, so it is obscure — but obscurity is not
144	a boundary, and the codebase already treats exactly this threat as real elsewhere
145	(`assertInternalGrowthCaller`, `lib/actions-growth.ts:11-30`).
146	
147	**Fix.** Move `verifyTotpForUser` into a plain (non-`"use server"`) module imported by the login
148	action, or gate it behind a short-lived signed "password stage passed" token plus the same rate limit
149	as `login`.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## P0-3. Stripe pays, nothing is provisioned — the webhook consumes the fulfilment signal
154	
155	**Files:** `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:19-22`, `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27-94`,
156	`lib/stripe.ts:192-244`
157	
158	`creditCheckoutSession()` is idempotent via a `UNIQUE(stripeSessionId)` index and returns `true` only
159	for the caller that actually inserted the row. That boolean is the *only* signal that a session is
160	newly paid — and the confirm route gates all three fulfilment actions on it:
161	
162	```ts
163	// app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27-44
164	const credited = await creditCheckoutSession(sessionId);
165	const order = await getCheckoutOrderIntent(sessionId);
166	if (order) {
167	  if (credited) { ...placeOrder(user, order.intent)... }
168	  return NextResponse.redirect(`${base}/dashboard/servers`);   // ← silent no-op path
169	}
170	```
171	
172	The webhook calls the same function and throws the result away:
173	
174	```ts
175	// app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21
176	await creditCheckoutSession(session.id);
177	```
178	
179	**Failure scenario 1 (race).** Customer completes Checkout for a $249 annual Max VPS. Stripe fires
180	`checkout.session.completed` and redirects the browser at essentially the same instant. The webhook's
181	insert wins; the confirm request gets `P2002` → `credited === false` → line 44 redirects to
182	`/dashboard/servers`, which is empty. $249 charged, $249 in the wallet, no server, no error, no
183	notification, no admin alert.
184	
185	**Failure scenario 2 (deterministic, 100% reproducible).** Customer pays, then closes the tab / loses
186	connectivity before `success_url` resolves. The confirm route is never called at all. Identical
187	outcome. Stripe's own guidance is explicit that a redirect must not be the fulfilment trigger.
188	
189	The same defect applies verbatim to paid **upgrades** (`confirm/route.ts:52-70`) and paid **disk
190	expansions** (`:76-94`) — card charged, wallet credited, `RESIZE`/`DISK_EXPAND` job never queued.
191	
192	Nothing reconciles this: `grep -rl stripe worker/` returns nothing. Both keys are set in `.env`, so
193	this is live.
194	
195	**Fix.** Extract a shared `fulfilCheckoutSession(sessionId)` called by **both** the webhook and the
196	confirm route, made idempotent on its own marker (a `FulfilledSession` row, or a unique
197	`Job.stripeSessionId`) rather than on the wallet-credit side effect. Add a worker sweep that lists
198	sessions `paid` in the last 24h carrying `nxeonOrder`/`nxeonResize`/`nxeonDiskExpand` metadata with no
199	corresponding Server/Job and fulfils or alerts.
200	
201	---
202	
203	## P0-4. `BACKUP_RESTORE` permanently destroys attached block-storage volumes
204	
205	**Files:** `worker/restore.ts:116-120`, `lib/actions-server-ops.ts:116-147`
206	
207	```ts
208	// worker/restore.ts:116-120
209	const restoreUpid = await conn.post(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu`, { vmid, archive: volid, force: 1 });
210	```
211	
212	There is **no volume guard anywhere** in `worker/restore.ts` or the calling action — both were read in
213	full; neither mentions volumes. Confirmed against the hypervisor source on this box:
214	
215	* `/usr/share/perl5/PVE/QemuServer.pm:7751` — `destroy_vm(...) if -f $vmcfgfn;` with the comment
216	  *"avoid zombie disks when restoring over an existing VM -> cleanup first"*.
217	* `/usr/share/perl5/PVE/QemuServer.pm:1877-1882` — `destroy_vm` uses `include_unused => 1` and frees
218	  **every** volume owned by that vmid, `unusedN` entries included.
219	
220	**Failure scenario, on live data.** Server `ggjgjhgjghh` (vmid 102, `autoBackup: true`) has volume
221	"size 60" `ATTACHED` as `vmdata:vm-102-disk-1`. The customer restores any backup taken before the
222	volume was attached → `qmrestore --force` → `destroy_vm` frees `vm-102-disk-1` → the customer's data is
223	gone. `Volume.diskName` still points at the dead volid and **billing continues**.
224	
225	The reinstall path has an explicit, well-reasoned guard for exactly this hazard
226	(`worker/index.ts:416-444`). Restore, which does the same thing to the same vmid, has none.
227	
228	**Fix.** Apply the reinstall guard to restore: refuse `BACKUP_RESTORE` while any `Volume` is pinned to
229	the server (`serverId` set, regardless of status), at both the action and the worker handler.
230	
231	---
232	
233	## P0-5. Same-OS reinstall wipes a DETACHED-but-pinned volume — guard asymmetry
234	
235	**Files:** `lib/actions.ts:465`, `worker/index.ts:428-430`, `worker/index.ts:357-360`,
236	`worker/volumes.ts:240`, `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:112`
237	
238	`volumeDetach` deliberately keeps `serverId` so the volume can be re-attached; it only flips status
239	(`worker/volumes.ts:240`). The **OS-change** path counts *all* pinned volumes and is correct:
240	
241	```ts
242	// lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:112
243	const pinnedVolumes = await db.volume.count({ where: { serverId } });
244	```
245	
246	The **same-OS "Reinstall"** path counts only `ATTACHED`, at both layers:
247	
248	```ts
249	// lib/actions.ts:465          and      worker/index.ts:428-430
250	db.volume.count({ where: { serverId, status: "ATTACHED" } })
251	```
252	
253	then:
254	
255	```ts
256	// worker/index.ts:357-360
257	const delUpid = await conn.del(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${vmid}`, {
258	  "destroy-unreferenced-disks": 1, purge: 1,
259	});
260	```
261	
262	**Failure scenario.** Customer attaches a volume, fills it, clicks **Detach** — the UI at
263	`components/customer/Volumes.tsx:173` promises *"Data is preserved."* — then clicks **Reinstall**. Both
264	guards see zero `ATTACHED` volumes and pass. `qm destroy --purge` frees the `unusedN` disk
265	(`QemuServer.pm:1877-1882`). Data gone. The code comment at `worker/index.ts:416-427` describes this
266	exact hazard; the filter it wrote doesn't cover it.
267	
268	**Fix.** Change both counts to `{ where: { serverId } }`, matching `reinstallToOs`.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## P0-6. Upgrade proration uses undiscounted list price — customers are overcharged
273

448	
449	**Files:** `worker/game-config.ts:243-249`, `:212-234`; `worker/index.ts:935`, `:1142`, `:1000`, `:1023`
450	
451	`worker/game-config.ts` holds the one exec helper in the tree that does **not reject on timeout**:
452	
453	```ts
454	const timer = setTimeout(() => {
455	  try { stream.close(); } catch { /* ignore */ }
456	}, EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS);
457	```
458	
459	It only closes the stream — if no `close` event follows (network partition, half-open TCP) the promise
460	never settles. Compare the correct pattern at `lib/ssh-exec.ts:121-130`, `worker/ssl.ts:83-90`,
461	`worker/migrate-real.ts:430-434`, which all set `settled` and `reject(...)`. `sftpRead`/`sftpWrite`
462	(`worker/game-config.ts:212-234`) have **no timeout at all**.
463	
464	Three amplifiers:
465	* `runJob` has **no wall-clock cap** — `worker/index.ts:935` is a bare `await handlers[job.type](job)`.
466	* The loop is strictly serial — `worker/index.ts:1142` `if (claimed) await runJob(claimed);` inside `for (;;)`.
467	* `reapStuckJobs()` is **startup-only** — defined at `:1000`, called once at `:1023`, nowhere else. No
468	  periodic reaper, no heartbeat.

470	**Failure scenario.** A customer saves game settings (`lib/actions-game-config.ts:112` enqueues
471	`GAME_CONFIG`) on a VM that goes network-dark mid-command. The job stays `RUNNING` forever and the
472	`for(;;)` loop never iterates again. **No other job runs for any customer** — no provisioning, no
473	deletes, no backups — and the billing, monitoring and renewal sweeps (`worker/index.ts:1034-1126`) stop
474	with it. Only a manual `systemctl restart nxeon-worker` clears it. Ironically `workerHealth()`
475	(`lib/monitoring.ts:262-289`) *would* detect this, but nothing acts on it.
476	
477	**Fix.** Make the game-config timeout `reject`; add timeouts to `sftpRead`/`sftpWrite`; wrap `runJob`
478	in a per-type wall-clock cap; run `reapStuckJobs()` on the sweep timer, not just at startup.

669	returns `{ suspended }`; `bulkVoidInvoices` skips PAID invoices and returns `{ voided, skipped }`.
670	
671	*Failure:* on `/admin/users` the admin selects 5 staff accounts and clicks Suspend → banner reads
672	**"Suspend: 5 rows done."** while zero were suspended. On `/admin/invoices`, selecting 20 invoices of
673	which 15 are PAID reports "Void: 20 rows done." when 5 were voided.
674	
675	## P1-14. Plan downgrades cannot succeed for any customer — the feature is inert
676	
677	**Files:** `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:163`, `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:88-96`
678	
679	The downgrade guard requires the target plan's disk to be `>=` the current plan's. Cross-checking the
680	**live** plan catalogue, every active plan is strictly ordered by both price and disk (Starter 25 GB /
681	$8.99 · Standard 50 GB / $12.99 · Pro 80 GB / $20.99 · Max 120 GB / $32.99), so there is **not one
682	valid downgrade pair**.
683	
684	*Failure:* a Max customer opens the "Downsize your plan" card, sees three cheaper plans rendered at
685	40% opacity with every button `disabled` and the submit button permanently greyed out. The empty-state
686	copy ("You're already on the smallest plan") only fires when there are no cheaper plans at all, so it
687	never shows. The feature is shipped, prominent, and impossible to use.
688	
689	## P1-15. `ResizeDown`'s displayed credit uses a third, different formula from the server
690	
691	**Files:** `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:49-59` vs `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:176-183`
692	
693	Client: `(vpsTermPriceCents(old) − vpsTermPriceCents(new)) × remainingFraction`, clamped to one term.
694	Server: `(old.priceCents − new.priceCents) × remainingMonths`, undiscounted and unclamped.
695	
696	For Max→Standard with 364 days left on an annual term the customer is shown **$215.41** and credited
697	**$239.16**. This directly violates the invariant the codebase states for every other money path
698	("the split the customer SEES is byte-for-byte the split that gets CHARGED",
699	`lib/wallet-split.ts:1-4`). Currently masked by P1-14.
700	
701	## P1-16. Detach hot-unplugs a mounted filesystem from a running VM
702	
703	**Files:** `lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-154`, `worker/volumes.ts:236`, `worker/product-renewals.ts:433-435`
704	
705	The only guard is `volume.status !== "ATTACHED"`. There is no `server.status` check — conspicuous,
706	because `attachVolume` has one (`lib/actions-volumes.ts:124`). The worker issues a live SCSI unplug
707	with no `fsfreeze`, `sync`, or guest-agent unmount; provision never sets `hotplug`
708	(`worker/index.ts:284-303`), so Proxmox's default `disk,network,usb` applies.
709	
710	*Failure:* volume mounted at `/var/lib/mysql`; customer clicks Detach (UI says *"Data is preserved"*);
711	the device vanishes mid-write → journal abort / InnoDB corruption. The same primitive fires **with no
712	human involved** from billing: `worker/product-renewals.ts:433-435` queues `VOLUME_DETACH` on an
713	overdue volume attached to a running VM.
714	
715	## P1-17. Re-attach with a lost `diskName` hands back a blank disk and orphans the data
716	
717	**Files:** `worker/volumes.ts:166`, `:199`, `:231`, `:240-248`; `worker/index.ts:432-436`
718	
719	```ts
720	const source = volume.diskName ? volume.diskName : `${storage}:${volume.sizeGB}`;
721	```
722	
723	No "was this attached before?" check. `worker/index.ts:432-436` proves null-`diskName` ATTACHED volumes
724	occur in production, and `worker/volumes.ts:172-175` documents the race that causes it.
725	
726	*Failure:* volume V (500 GB of data) has `diskName === null`. Detach → `:231` `if (server?.vmid &&
727	volume.diskName)` is false so nothing is unplugged, but `:240` flips to DETACHED and `:242-248`
728	notifies *"data are preserved."* Re-attach → line 166 creates a **brand-new empty 500 GB disk** and
729	`:199` overwrites `diskName`. The customer sees an unformatted disk; the real zvol is orphaned with no
730	DB reference.
731	
732	## P1-18. `Node.natChain` / `subnetPrefix` are validated, stored, and ignored by the worker
733	
734	**Files:** `lib/actions-nodes.ts:21, :128-131, :174-200`; `worker/network.ts:7, :32-54`;
735	`app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx:24-25`
736	
737	`natChain` is documented as *"the iptables chain the worker rebuilds from the DB"* and is enforced
738	globally unique. But `worker/network.ts:7` hardcodes `process.env.NXEON_NAT_CHAIN ?? "NXEON_FWD"`, and
739	`syncPortForwards()` selects **every** server regardless of node and DNATs them all into that one
740	chain. `Node.natChain` has no consumer anywhere.
741	
742	*Failure:* admin registers node-2 via `/admin/nodes/new` and provisions a VM there (guest
743	`10.20.1.101`). The worker flushes `NXEON_FWD` **on the primary host** and adds a DNAT to an address
744	that host cannot route. `NXEON_FWD_N2` is never created on node-2. Every node-2 VM has dead SSH while
745	`/admin/nodes` shows the node green/ONLINE.
746	
747	*Compounding:* `updateNode` (`:174-200`) lets an admin change `subnetPrefix`, `ipStart/ipEnd`,
748	`natChain` and `bridge` on a node that already has servers — no `_count.servers` guard (only
749	`deleteNode:292` has one). Editing the subnet on the live primary makes `lib/ipam.ts:168` stop seeing
750	existing leases, and the next provision hands out an IP already in use.

752	## P1-19. Team RBAC (`Membership.areas`) is computed, stored, and never enforced
753	
754	**Files:** `lib/team-guard.ts:16`, `lib/team-areas.ts:71, :103`, `lib/actions-teams.ts:195`,
755	`app/dashboard/team/page.tsx:48`
756	
757	`requireArea(orgId, area)` has **zero call sites anywhere in the repo**. `memberCanAccess` is
758	referenced only from inside `team-guard.ts` itself; `memberCanAccessHref` is never called.
759	`setMemberAreas` writes the field, the UI renders it, nothing reads it back.
760

762	joins `Membership` to servers/domains/invoices). But an operator who restricts a viewer to
763	`["invoices"]` gets a UI that says the restriction is in force when it is not, and the moment
764	org-shared resources land this becomes a live hole.

766	## P1-20. No first-purchase invoice for four product lines

768	**Verified by mapping every `invoiceCreateData` / `createInvoice` call site.** Invoices are created for
769	VPS orders, VPS renewals, resizes, disk expansions, domain transfers-in, domain *auto*-renewals and

788	`assertInternalGrowthCaller` permits an action-dispatched call when `real.id === userId`. But the

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — customer VM backups via vzdump
# Backs up all QEMU guests (running or stopped) with VMID in [100, 9000)
# to Proxmox storage "backup" using zstd compression, snapshot mode, keeping
# the last 3 backups per VM at the storage level. Templates (9000-9999) are
# excluded. Idempotent / re-runnable.
set -euo pipefail

STORAGE="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE:-backup}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

# Collect eligible VMIDs: numeric first column of `qm list`, VMID>=100, <9000.
mapfile -t VMIDS < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}' | sort -n)

if [ "${#VMIDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "no eligible VMs (none with 100 <= VMID < 9000); nothing to back up"
    exit 0
fi

log "eligible customer VMs: ${VMIDS[*]}"

# Optional dry-run: NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN=1 only prints the selection/command.
if [ "${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    log "DRY RUN — would run: vzdump ${VMIDS[*]} --storage ${STORAGE} --compress zstd --mode snapshot --prune-backups keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"
    exit 0
fi

log "running vzdump -> storage '${STORAGE}' (zstd, snapshot, keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"
vzdump "${VMIDS[@]}" \
    --storage "$STORAGE" \
    --compress zstd \
    --mode snapshot \
    --prune-backups "keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"

log "done"

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — PostgreSQL logical backups
# pg_dumps both databases (nxeon, nxeon_staging) as the postgres user to
# /tank/backup/db/, gzip-compressed with timestamped filenames, and prunes
# dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS. Idempotent / re-runnable.
set -euo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
RETENTION_DAYS="${NXEON_DB_RETENTION_DAYS:-14}"
DATABASES=(nxeon nxeon_staging)
TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

rc=0
for db in "${DATABASES[@]}"; do
    # Skip cleanly if the database does not exist (e.g. staging removed).
    if ! sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='${db}'" | grep -q 1; then
        log "database '${db}' not present, skipping"
        continue
    fi

    dest="${BACKUP_DIR}/${db}-${TS}.sql.gz"
    tmp="${dest}.partial"
    log "dumping '${db}' -> ${dest}"
    if sudo -u postgres pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges "$db" | gzip -c > "$tmp"; then
        mv "$tmp" "$dest"
        # Integrity check: gzip stream must decompress cleanly.
        if gunzip -t "$dest"; then
            log "OK ${dest} ($(du -h "$dest" | cut -f1))"
        else
            log "ERROR gunzip -t failed for ${dest}"
            rc=1
        fi
    else
        log "ERROR pg_dump failed for '${db}'"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        rc=1
    fi
done

# Prune dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS.
log "pruning dumps older than ${RETENTION_DAYS} days in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql.gz' -mtime "+${RETENTION_DAYS}" -print -delete || true

log "done (exit ${rc})"
exit "$rc"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Off-box backup replication.
#
# Copies /tank/backup/db (and optionally VM dumps) to an OFFSITE target so a
# chassis/disk loss doesn't take the backups with it. Inert until configured —
# set ONE of the following in /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env:
#
#   OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups"     # rclone remote (Backblaze B2, S3, OVH Object Storage…)
#   OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="user@host:/backups/nxeon"   # rsync over SSH (rsync.net etc.)
#   OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1                        # optional: also replicate VM dumps (large)
#
# Exits non-zero on a real failure so the systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins.
set -uo pipefail

ENV_FILE="/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env"
SRC_DB="/tank/backup/db"
SRC_VMS="/tank/backup/dump"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }

[ -f "${ENV_FILE}" ] && . "${ENV_FILE}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore-verification: proves the newest production dump is actually restorable.
#
# Restores the latest /tank/backup/db/nxeon-*.sql.gz into a scratch database,
# asserts that core tables restored with rows, then drops the scratch database.
# Production data is never touched. Exits non-zero on any failure so the
# systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins.
set -uo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
SCRATCH="nxeon_restore_verify"
LOG="/tmp/nxeon-verify-restore.log"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }
fail() { log "FAIL: $*"; sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1; exit 1; }

LATEST="$(ls -1t "${BACKUP_DIR}"/nxeon-*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
[ -n "${LATEST}" ] || fail "no production dump found in ${BACKUP_DIR}"

AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${LATEST}") ) / 3600 ))
log "verifying ${LATEST} (age ${AGE_H}h, $(stat -c%s "${LATEST}") bytes)"
[ "${AGE_H}" -lt 48 ] || log "WARNING: newest dump is ${AGE_H}h old (>48h)"

# gzip integrity first — a corrupt archive should fail loudly.
gzip -t "${LATEST}" || fail "gzip integrity check failed"

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
sudo -u postgres psql -qc "CREATE DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null || fail "could not create scratch db"

if ! zcat "${LATEST}" | sudo -u postgres psql -q "${SCRATCH}" >"${LOG}" 2>&1; then
  log "psql restore returned non-zero; see ${LOG}"
fi
ERRS=$(grep -ci '^ERROR' "${LOG}" || true)
[ "${ERRS}" -eq 0 ] || { log "restore produced ${ERRS} errors:"; grep -i '^ERROR' "${LOG}" | head -5; fail "restore had errors"; }

# Core tables must exist and hold rows — an empty "successful" restore is a failure.
for t in User OsTemplate Plan; do
  n=$(sudo -u postgres psql -tA "${SCRATCH}" -c "select count(*) from \"${t}\";" 2>/dev/null || echo "x")
  [[ "${n}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "table ${t} missing from restored dump"
  [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] || fail "table ${t} restored with 0 rows"
  log "OK ${t}=${n}"
done

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null
log "restore verification PASSED (scratch db dropped, production untouched)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nxeon — host configuration backup (the bare-metal rebuild set).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: nothing on this box backed up /etc/pve. The VM *disks* were
# being dumped by vzdump, but /etc/pve/qemu-server/<vmid>.conf — the file that
# says how much RAM a guest has, which bridge and MAC its NIC uses, which disks
# it owns and in what order, plus /etc/pve/storage.cfg, /etc/pve/user.cfg and the
# firewall rules — existed in exactly one place: this chassis. After a total host
# loss you would have had a directory full of vzdump archives and no VM
# definitions to restore them into, no storage named `vmdata` for them to land
# on, and no record of the network layout. `qmrestore` reads the config out of
# the archive for the guest itself, but the *host* side (storage.cfg, bridges,
# users, ACLs, the Nxeon systemd units) would have had to be reconstructed from
# memory. This script is small, fast (~16 KB of config) and runs before the
# multi-gigabyte guest dumps so the cheapest, most irreplaceable data is
# captured first.
#
# Also snapshots the *interpretation* of that config (pvesm status, pveversion,
# zpool status, ip addr) as plain text, because a rebuild is done by a human
# reading it, not only by a machine restoring it.
#
# Idempotent / re-runnable. Deletes nothing except its own aged-out archives.
set -uo pipefail

DEST_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_CONFIG_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"
TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
DEST="${DEST_DIR}/host-config-${TS}.tar.gz"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }

mkdir -p "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" || { log "FAIL: cannot create ${DEST_DIR}"; exit 1; }
chmod 755 "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true

if [ ! -d /etc/pve ]; then
    log "FAIL: /etc/pve does not exist — is this a Proxmox host?"
    exit 1
fi

# Plain-text state snapshots, gathered into the archive alongside the raw config.
# A rebuilder needs to know what the pools/versions/interfaces *were*, and none of
# that is recoverable from /etc/pve alone.
work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-config-backup.XXXXXX)" || { log "FAIL: mktemp"; exit 1; }
trap 'rm -rf "${work}"' EXIT
snap="${work}/state"
mkdir -p "${snap}"

{
    echo "# Nxeon host state snapshot — ${TS}"
    echo "# hostname: $(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
} > "${snap}/README.txt"

pveversion -v            >"${snap}/pveversion.txt"      2>&1 || true
pvesm status             >"${snap}/pvesm-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
qm list                  >"${snap}/qm-list.txt"         2>&1 || true
zpool status             >"${snap}/zpool-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
zfs list -o name,used,avail,mountpoint >"${snap}/zfs-list.txt" 2>&1 || true
ip -o addr               >"${snap}/ip-addr.txt"         2>&1 || true
ip route                 >"${snap}/ip-route.txt"        2>&1 || true
iptables-save            >"${snap}/iptables-save.txt"   2>&1 || true
systemctl list-unit-files 'nxeon*' --no-legend >"${snap}/nxeon-units.txt" 2>&1 || true
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT >"${snap}/lsblk.txt" 2>&1 || true

# What goes in. Every path here is either irreplaceable (VM definitions, cluster
# keys, TLS material, the panel's own env) or expensive to reconstruct by hand.
PATHS=(
    /etc/pve                        # VM/CT definitions, storage.cfg, user.cfg, firewall, priv/
    /etc/nxeon                      # panel env: offsite target, Cloudflare, mail, TLS
    /etc/network/interfaces         # bridges the guests are attached to
    /etc/hostname
    /etc/hosts
    /etc/fstab
    /etc/resolv.conf
)
# Optional extras — included only if present, never a reason to fail.
for p in /etc/nginx /etc/postfix /etc/apt/sources.list /etc/apt/sources.list.d /var/spool/cron/crontabs; do
    [ -e "$p" ] && PATHS+=("$p")
done
# The Nxeon systemd units themselves (service/timer/drop-in), collected by glob.
mapfile -t NXEON_UNITS < <(find /etc/systemd/system -maxdepth 2 -name 'nxeon-*' 2>/dev/null)

tmp="${DEST}.partial"
# 0600 from the moment it exists: this archive contains /etc/pve/priv (cluster and
# CA keys) and /etc/nxeon (API tokens, mail credentials). It must never be
# world-readable on a 0755 directory.
( umask 077
  tar -czf "${tmp}" \
      --warning=no-file-changed --warning=no-file-ignored \
      -C "${work}" state \
      "${PATHS[@]}" "${NXEON_UNITS[@]}" 2>"${work}/tar.err" )
rc=$?

# tar exit 1 == "some files changed while reading" (normal for the pmxcfs FUSE
# mount and for live logs). Only exit >= 2 is a real failure.
if [ "${rc}" -ge 2 ] || [ ! -s "${tmp}" ]; then
    log "FAIL: tar exited ${rc}"
    sed -n '1,20p' "${work}/tar.err" 2>/dev/null | while read -r l; do log "  tar: ${l}"; done
    rm -f "${tmp}"
    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"tar exited %s"}\n' "$(date -Is)" "${rc}" \
        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
fi
[ "${rc}" -eq 1 ] && log "note: tar reported files changed during read (expected for /etc/pve)"

mv "${tmp}" "${DEST}"
chmod 600 "${DEST}"

# Integrity check: an archive that cannot be listed is not a backup. Assert the
# VM definitions are actually inside it — a silently empty tarball that reports
# success is the failure mode this whole file exists to prevent.
if ! tar -tzf "${DEST}" >"${work}/list.txt" 2>&1; then
    log "FAIL: ${DEST} is not a readable gzip archive"
    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"archive unreadable"}\n' "$(date -Is)" \
        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
fi
confs=$(grep -c 'etc/pve/qemu-server/.*\.conf$' "${work}/list.txt" || true)
if [ "${confs}" -lt 1 ]; then
    log "FAIL: ${DEST} contains no /etc/pve/qemu-server/*.conf — VM definitions missing"
    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"no VM definitions in archive"}\n' "$(date -Is)" \
        > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
    chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
fi

size=$(stat -c%s "${DEST}")
log "OK ${DEST} ($(du -h "${DEST}" | cut -f1), ${confs} VM definition(s))"

# Retention: keep the newest KEEP_LAST host-config archives. Scoped by an exact
# filename pattern in one directory, so it can only ever match archives this
# script wrote — never a vzdump archive, never a customer's anything.
mapfile -t old < <(ls -1t "${DEST_DIR}"/host-config-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | tail -n "+$((KEEP_LAST + 1))")
for f in "${old[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "${f}" ] || continue
    log "pruning ${f} (keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"
    rm -f -- "${f}"
done

printf '{"ok":true,"at":"%s","archive":"%s","bytes":%s,"vmDefinitions":%s,"keepLast":%s}\n' \
    "$(date -Is)" "${DEST}" "${size}" "${confs}" "${KEEP_LAST}" \
    > "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json"
chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/host-config.json" 2>/dev/null || true

log "done"

# the backups with it.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHY THIS NOW FAILS INSTEAD OF EXITING 0

# -07-25 and -07-26 and recorded `Result=success` every time, having copied
# nothing anywhere. systemd showed a green unit, the OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook
# never fired because nothing failed, and the admin portal had no page that would
# have said otherwise. For three days the platform reported working off-site
# backups while every byte it owned lived on one pool in one chassis.
#
# An inert backup that reports OK is worse than no backup at all: no backup at
# least leaves the operator's belief accurate. So an unconfigured target is now a
# hard failure — non-zero exit, systemd unit red, admin notification via
# nxeon-alert@ — and it stays red until someone actually configures a target or
# explicitly, deliberately acknowledges the risk.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THE OWNER MUST SET
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edit /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env and set exactly ONE of:
#
#   OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups"
#       An rclone remote (Backblaze B2, S3, OVH/Hetzner object storage, Google
#       Drive…). Requires: apt install rclone && rclone config  — configure the
#       remote as ROOT, because this unit runs as root and reads root's
#       ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf.
#

#       rsync over SSH (rsync.net, a second box, a NAS). Requires key-based auth
#       for root with no passphrase prompt: ssh-keygen, then ssh-copy-id, then
#       verify `ssh -o BatchMode=yes user@host true` succeeds as root.
#

#   OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1        also replicate the whole-system VM archives.
#                                Large (tens of GB/day) but this is the only copy
#                                that survives losing the chassis. Strongly
#                                recommended once bandwidth allows.
#   OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1      acknowledge "no off-site copy exists" and exit 0.
#                                ONLY for a deliberately single-chassis
#                                deployment. This is the switch that turns the
#                                alarm off; there is no other.

# private keys) and /etc/nxeon (Proxmox API token, Cloudflare token, mail
# credentials). Whatever target you choose is now a copy of the keys to this

SRC_DB="/tank/backup/db"

    log "  OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET=\"user@host:/backups/nxeon\"  (root key-based SSH, BatchMode must work)"
    log ""

    log "If this host is deliberately single-chassis, set OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1"
    log "to acknowledge the risk and silence this failure. Do not silence it by"
    log "any other means: this unit reporting success while copying nothing is"
    log "exactly the state it spent 2026-07-24..26 in."
    log "=============================================================="

    write_status false true ambiguous "both rclone and rsync targets are set"
    exit 1

    log "FAIL: ${SRC_DB} missing — there is nothing to replicate, which is itself a problem"
    write_status false true "${KIND}" "source ${SRC_DB} missing"
    exit 1

# files. A transport that exits 0 without transferring anything (wrong remote
# path, silently empty source, an rclone remote pointing at a deleted bucket) is
# the same class of lie this script was rewritten to stop telling.
sync_one() {
    local src="$1" label="$2" rc=0
    local n_src
    n_src=$(find "${src}" -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name '*.partial' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    if [ "${n_src}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "FAIL: ${label}: source ${src} holds no files — refusing to report a successful sync"
        return 1
    fi

    if [ "${KIND}" = "rclone" ]; then
        command -v rclone >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rclone not installed (apt install rclone)"; return 1; }
        log "rclone sync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <remote>/${label}"
        rclone sync "${src}" "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" \
            --transfers 4 --retries 3 --exclude '*.partial' || rc=$?
        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rclone exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
        # Post-sync assertion: the remote must now list files.
        local n_dst
        n_dst=$(rclone lsf "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
            log "FAIL: ${label}: remote lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
            return 1
        fi
        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the remote)"
    else
        command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rsync not installed"; return 1; }
        log "rsync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <target>/${label}"
        rsync -az --delete --exclude '*.partial' \
            -e "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=20" \
            "${src}/" "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}/${label}/" || rc=$?
        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rsync exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
        # Post-sync assertion: count files on the far side over the same transport.
        local host="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET%%:*}" path="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET#*:}" n_dst
        n_dst=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 "${host}" \
            "find '${path}/${label}' -maxdepth 1 -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
            log "FAIL: ${label}: target lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
            return 1
        fi
        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the target)"
    fi
}

fail=0
synced=""

sync_one "${SRC_DB}" "db" && synced="${synced}db " || fail=1

# The host-configuration archives are ~50 KB and are the difference between
# "restore the VMs" and "rebuild every VM definition from memory". They are
# replicated unconditionally: there is no bandwidth argument against 50 KB.
if [ -d "${SRC_PLATFORM}" ] && find "${SRC_PLATFORM}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'host-config-*.tar.gz' | read -r _; then

        fail=1
    fi
else

fi

    fi

    log "note: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS is not set — VM archives are NOT replicated off-site."
    log "      A chassis loss would still cost every VM image. Set OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 when bandwidth allows."
fi

    log "off-site replication FAILED"
    exit 1
fi

write_status true true "${KIND}" "replicated: ${synced% }"
log "off-site replication complete (${synced% })"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore-verification: proves the newest backups are actually restorable.
#
#   Part 1 (destructive-proof): restores the latest /tank/backup/db/nxeon-*.sql.gz
#           into a scratch database and asserts core tables came back with rows.
#   Part 2 (structural): asserts the whole-system side exists and is fresh — a
#           host-config archive that lists real VM definitions, and a recent VM
#           archive per guest. Part 2 is why this script no longer only proves the
#           database is safe: on 2026-07-26 the DB half had been green for days
#           while the whole-VM half had literally never produced a single archive,
#           and this script could not have told anyone.
#
# Production data is never touched. Exits non-zero on any failure so the systemd
# OnFailure hook alerts admins. Also writes a status file for /admin/backups —
# without it the panel can only report "the unit exited 0", which is precisely the
# signal that proved worthless for the off-site job.
set -uo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
PLATFORM_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
STATUS="${STATUS_DIR}/verify-restore.json"
SCRATCH="nxeon_restore_verify"
LOG="/tmp/nxeon-verify-restore.log"
MAX_AGE_H="${NXEON_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS:-48}"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }

mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true

WARNINGS=""
warn() { log "WARNING: $*"; WARNINGS="${WARNINGS}${WARNINGS:+; }$*"; }

write_status() {
    printf '{"ok":%s,"at":"%s","dbDump":"%s","dbAgeHours":%s,"vmArchives":%s,"vmNewestAgeHours":%s,"hostConfigVmDefs":%s,"warnings":"%s","error":%s}\n' \
        "$1" "$(date -Is)" "${DB_DUMP_NAME:-}" "${DB_AGE_H:--1}" "${VM_ARCHIVES:--1}" \
        "${VM_AGE_H:--1}" "${CONF_DEFS:--1}" "${WARNINGS}" "$2" > "${STATUS}"
    chmod 644 "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

fail() {
    log "FAIL: $*"
    sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
    write_status false "\"$*\""
    exit 1
}

DB_DUMP_NAME=""; DB_AGE_H=-1; VM_ARCHIVES=-1; VM_AGE_H=-1; CONF_DEFS=-1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1 — the database dump really restores
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
LATEST="$(ls -1t "${BACKUP_DIR}"/nxeon-*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
[ -n "${LATEST}" ] || fail "no production dump found in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
DB_DUMP_NAME="$(basename "${LATEST}")"

DB_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${LATEST}") ) / 3600 ))
log "verifying ${LATEST} (age ${DB_AGE_H}h, $(stat -c%s "${LATEST}") bytes)"
[ "${DB_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest DB dump is ${DB_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h)"

# gzip integrity first — a corrupt archive should fail loudly.
gzip -t "${LATEST}" || fail "gzip integrity check failed"

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
sudo -u postgres psql -qc "CREATE DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null || fail "could not create scratch db"

if ! zcat "${LATEST}" | sudo -u postgres psql -q "${SCRATCH}" >"${LOG}" 2>&1; then
  log "psql restore returned non-zero; see ${LOG}"
fi
ERRS=$(grep -ci '^ERROR' "${LOG}" || true)
[ "${ERRS}" -eq 0 ] || { log "restore produced ${ERRS} errors:"; grep -i '^ERROR' "${LOG}" | head -5; fail "restore had errors"; }

# Core tables must exist and hold rows — an empty "successful" restore is a failure.
for t in User OsTemplate Plan Server; do
  n=$(sudo -u postgres psql -tA "${SCRATCH}" -c "select count(*) from \"${t}\";" 2>/dev/null || echo "x")
  [[ "${n}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "table ${t} missing from restored dump"
  [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] || fail "table ${t} restored with 0 rows"
  log "OK ${t}=${n}"
done

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null
log "DB restore verification PASSED (scratch db dropped, production untouched)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 2 — the whole-system side exists and is fresh
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Not a real restore: qmrestore of a 10 GB guest onto a live host is not something
# a weekly timer should do unsupervised. What it DOES assert is everything that was
# false on this box for its first four days of life — that host-level archives
# exist at all, that they are recent, that one exists per running guest, and that
# the host-config tarball actually contains VM definitions rather than being an
# empty tarball that reported success.
CONF="$(ls -1t "${PLATFORM_DIR}"/host-config-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -z "${CONF}" ]; then
    fail "no host-config-*.tar.gz in ${PLATFORM_DIR} — /etc/pve is not backed up, a bare-metal rebuild would have no VM definitions"
fi
CONF_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${CONF}") ) / 3600 ))
CONF_DEFS=$(tar -tzf "${CONF}" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE 'etc/pve/(nodes/[^/]+/)?qemu-server/[0-9]+\.conf$' || true)
[ "${CONF_DEFS}" -gt 0 ] || fail "$(basename "${CONF}") contains no VM definitions"
log "OK host config $(basename "${CONF}") (age ${CONF_AGE_H}h, ${CONF_DEFS} VM definition(s))"
[ "${CONF_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest host-config archive is ${CONF_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h)"

VM_ARCHIVES=$(find "${PLATFORM_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'vzdump-*.vma*' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
if [ "${VM_ARCHIVES}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "no whole-system VM archives in ${PLATFORM_DIR} — the nxeon-backup-vms timer has produced nothing"
fi
NEWEST_VM="$(ls -1t "${PLATFORM_DIR}"/vzdump-*.vma* 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
VM_AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${NEWEST_VM}") ) / 3600 ))
log "OK ${VM_ARCHIVES} VM archive(s) present, newest $(basename "${NEWEST_VM}") (age ${VM_AGE_H}h)"
[ "${VM_AGE_H}" -lt "${MAX_AGE_H}" ] || warn "newest VM archive is ${VM_AGE_H}h old (>${MAX_AGE_H}h) — the daily backup is not running"

# Per-guest coverage: a running guest with no archive is invisible in an aggregate
# count. This is how "the platform has 40 archives" can still mean "vmid 104 has
# never been backed up".
while read -r vmid; do
    [ -n "${vmid}" ] || continue
    if ! compgen -G "${PLATFORM_DIR}/vzdump-qemu-${vmid}-*.vma*" >/dev/null; then
        warn "guest ${vmid} has NO whole-system archive"
    fi
done < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}')

if [ -n "${WARNINGS}" ]; then
    log "restore verification PASSED WITH WARNINGS: ${WARNINGS}"
else
    log "restore verification PASSED (database restorable; whole-system archives present and fresh)"
fi
write_status true null
